title: Non-Surgical BBL: What Works and What the FDA Warns About
meta_description: No injection is FDA approved to enlarge the buttocks, and the FDA recommends against fillers for it. What each non-surgical BBL option can and can't do.
excerpt: The FDA has not approved any injectable filler for body contouring, and it recommends against using fillers to enlarge the buttocks. Here is what the sources say about fillers, silicone, Sculptra, devices and training, and what to do if you have already had injections.
quick_answer:
Is there a non-surgical BBL?

Not one the FDA has approved. The FDA says it has not approved injectable silicone or any injectable fillers for body contouring or enhancement, and it recommends against using them to increase the size of the buttocks. Glute training can build muscle, but lasting volume from your own fat takes surgery, which has its own risks.

Non-surgical BBL options: what to know
Butt fillers | The FDA recommends against them to increase the size of the buttocks
Injectable silicone | Not approved for any aesthetic procedure, the FDA says
Sculptra | Off-label on the buttocks, with small studies
Glute training | Builds muscle, not fat volume
Padded shapewear | Changes your outline only while you wear it
Sources: FDA; Frontiers in Physiology
